findings.text: The fragment states that the compare.py check 'requires every moved cell to be in the mask and reported no violation on either host'. That is not what the record shows for the fleet host: the fleet (Broadwell) comparison ran at 11:35 with the pre-fix comparator, which thresholded the whole-array maximum relative difference rather than the outside-mask maximum, and its only recorded output is 'violations [{cell_current, outside_conic: [], max_rel 1.544e-11}, {radial_moment, outside_conic: [], 1.972e-11}, {vertical_moment, outside_conic: [], 8.970e-07}]' with EXIT=1. compare.py was then corrected (the committed version computes outside_max_rel) and only the sirius arm was re-run with it. The substantive claim still holds: the empty outside_conic lists, and the printed moved_cell_ids for all three fields (all inside the 29-cell conic mask), are in that same log, so no cell outside the mask moved on either host. What is wrong is the sentence asserting a guard verdict the run did not give; a reader would take it as a second firing of the corrected check that never happened.

The script the manifest records in the tests field ends with a hardcoded 'echo EXIT=0', so re-running that exact command reports success whatever the arms do; the per-arm EXIT=1/EXIT=0 lines the manifest actually relies on were assembled by a helper that lives only in the run's scratch tree and is not committed. Measured on the reviewed run's own base arm: four arms ran, the booking arm failed with '1 failed, 4 passed' and EXIT=1, and the script's own final line would still be EXIT=0. A gate whose command cannot show a failure is the fail-open shape the evidence contract forbids; it should propagate the worst per-file status (or the summary assembly should be committed beside it).

The new preconditioner assertion establishes that the applied block inverse is A permutation (entries in {0,1}, unit row and column sums) but not that it is the IDENTITY permutation the brief asked for and the comment at line 578 ('only because this matrix's block inverse is an orthogonal permutation') claims. I confirmed by direct evaluation at the reviewed head that the applied matrix for this test's matrix is exactly the 24x24 identity, so the specialisation holds today and the assertion passes. But if the test matrix drifted so the block inverse became a non-identity permutation the assertion would stay green and the raw-matrix Arnoldi reference would be comparing against a different operator; only the separate 'error <= 1e-10' bound would catch it, and that is an agreement tolerance rather than a stated condition. The brief specified the identity; the assertion is one term short of it (e.g. np.array_equal(applied, np.eye(size))).

The comparator has no positive control: if both npz files were the same arm, or a field were absent or identically zero, it would report zero moved cells, no violations and EXIT=0, which reads as a clean verdict from an instrument that may not be looking. The repository already owns this idiom next door: scripts/prototypes/bank_booking_determinism/compare.py carries a nextafter perturbation positive control before it trusts any equality. The same file's difference()/fingerprint() are the numeric-difference and sha256 primitives this file re-derives instead of importing, for the same objects (booking receipt arrays in npz); the per-cell conic-mask confinement is genuinely new, so the addition is a fork with an extension rather than a pure copy.
